safe_upgrade_plan: The GPT edges, sfdisk layouts, complete Asahi ESP, and Linux GRUB configuration are copied and checksum-verified at /tmp/jwm1-native-preflight-recovery-20260905 on this CT.
The one-shot macOS selector was exercised and the machine returned to persistent Asahi after inspection; repeat it only after the backup blocker is cleared.
Time Machine currently cannot provide a restorable backup path. Reconnect or create an off-device backup and require concrete latestbackup/listbackups output before installation.
Live macOS reports 111689003008 bytes free. The signed Sonoma 14.8.9 package is 13654790295 bytes and the 38 GB Asahi reserve is present.
Use signed macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 build 23J631, which explicitly supports J293AP and is the smallest major-version change that meets MLX's macOS 14 floor.

Because a major upgrade can use several reboots, do not assume the one-shot selector will keep choosing macOS throughout installation. Before starting the installer, select Macintosh HD as the temporary Startup Disk and keep local console access available.
Complete the macOS upgrade without deleting, resizing, repairing, or reformatting any Asahi partition.
After the final macOS boot, verify macOS >=14, arm64, SDK >=14, and xcrun Metal availability with the recorded post-upgrade checks.

Fetch the exact mlx.lock archive, verify SHA-256 cb988a5bdc38c798918d042b9b1c6edda3ccc5f23a2155138d3aa5c1b2acc301, build in a fresh Python >=3.10 environment with setuptools >=80 and CMake >=3.25, and record native provenance before any comparison.
Return to Asahi through Startup Options, then restore the persistent Asahi target by name with asahi-bless after Linux boots. Do not select the stale one-core ANE GRUB entry.
rollback_plan: Before the macOS installer starts, a failed prerequisite check is a clean stop: power off and boot Asahi; the one-shot macOS selection does not replace the persistent Asahi target.

If macOS upgrades but the selected startup volume changes, hold the power button to open Startup Options and select Asahi Alarm Minimal (BTRFS). Once Linux boots, use 'sudo asahi-bless --set-boot "Asahi Alarm Minimal (BTRFS)" -y' and verify with 'sudo asahi-bless --get-boot'.

If Linux does not boot, use Startup Options to boot Macintosh HD or Options/RecoveryOS. Preserve all Asahi partitions; use the official Asahi installer from macOS for m1n1 repair rather than repartitioning.
If macOS data recovery is required, restore from the verified off-device backup. The same-disk Btrfs snapshot is not a macOS rollback.

Do not promise or attempt an ordinary firmware downgrade to Ventura. The Asahi platform guidance states system-global firmware normally moves only forward; a full DFU erase is a destructive last resort outside this plan.
